capability_matrix.notes: The observed Codex pair uses initialize plus session state; the final next protocol removes the handshake and protocol session.
The isolated Python MCP 2.0.0 KAG adapter and stable Codex 0.147.0 lab pair served server/discover; the production registration remains on 2025-11-25.

The isolated read-only KAG requestState handle passed bearer principal isolation, expiry, cross-request replay denial, tamper denial, and key-retirement revocation; same-request replay is allowed only for the idempotent read pilot.
The isolated KAG adapter proved self-describing requests across two clients with no session header or server-request backchannel; explicit application handles remain unproved.
The isolated KAG adapter preserved traceparent at pair level; trace metadata remains observation only and never becomes owner authority.

The isolated KAG pair proved private TTL hits, exact-expiry refetch, subscription addition invalidation, removal revocation, no-listener staleness, explicit refresh, and that stale discovery cannot authorize a removed tool.
Tasks is a separate extension and cannot be inferred from core support; Python MCP 2.0.0 explicitly does not implement the 2026-07-28 Tasks extension.
Next marks the legacy core features deprecated; removal is not implied.
Next widens tool schemas and output values; depth, external refs, and validator budgets need pair tests.

claim_limits: Protocol literals in a binary do not prove negotiated wire support.
A stable SDK release does not prove Codex pair support.
Official conformance does not prove Abyss owner, freshness, effect, or rollback behavior.
A read canary does not admit candidate or effect organs.
A registered alias does not prove schema observation or a grounded call.
Final publication and stable SDKs never authorize production migration without exact pair receipts.
